title: 02. Data Structures: Set Comprehension — Deduplication Patterns
summary: In real applications, data comes from multiple sources — databases, APIs, user inputs, files. Duplicates are everywhere.

sections.title: Explanation — Junior Developer Style
sections.body:
### Why Deduplication Matters

In real applications, data comes from **multiple sources** — databases, APIs, user inputs, files. **Duplicates are everywhere**. Set comprehensions give you the **fastest deduplication tool** in Python.

```python
# Pattern 1: Simple deduplication
data = [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]
unique = {x for x in data}   # {1, 2, 3}

# Pattern 2: Normalize then deduplicate (most useful!)
emails = ['Alice@Gmail.COM', 'alice@gmail.com', 'ALICE@GMAIL.COM']
unique_emails = {e.lower().strip() for e in emails}
# {'alice@gmail.com'}  ← All three were the same email!

# Pattern 3: Extract unique sub-elements
orders = [['apple', 'banana'], ['banana', 'cherry'], ['apple', 'cherry']]
all_items = {item for order in orders for item in order}
# {'apple', 'banana', 'cherry'}  ← Flat and unique!
```

### The Three Deduplication Strategies

```
Strategy 1: EXACT deduplication   → {x for x in data}
Strategy 2: NORMALIZED dedup      → {normalize(x) for x in data}
Strategy 3: FIELD-BASED dedup     → {x['key'] for x in data}
```

sections.title: 5 Examples
sections.body:
### Example 1: Customer Deduplication

```python
# Real scenario: merge customer lists from multiple sources

# Customers from CRM (might have duplicates across systems)
crm_customers = [
    'alice@company.com', 'BOB@Company.COM', 'carol@company.com',
    'dave@company.com', 'Alice@Company.com'
]
email_list_customers = [
    'bob@company.com', 'carol@company.com', 'eve@company.com',
    'FRANK@company.com', 'alice@company.com'
]
manual_entries = [
    '  grace@company.com ', ' DAVE@company.com', 'henry@company.com'
]

# All sources combined
all_sources = crm_customers + email_list_customers + manual_entries

# Deduplicate with normalization (strip + lowercase)
unique_customers = {email.strip().lower() for email in all_sources}

print(f"Total entries across sources: {len(all_sources)}")
print(f"Unique customers: {len(unique_customers)}")
print("Unique list:")
for email in sorted(unique_customers):
    print(f"  {email}")

# Total entries across sources: 15
# Unique customers: 8
# alice@company.com, bob@company.com, carol@company.com, ...
```

### Example 2: Product SKU Deduplication

```python
# E-commerce: products from multiple vendor feeds

vendor_feeds = {
    'vendor_a': [
        {'sku': 'PROD-001', 'name': 'Widget A', 'price': 9.99},
        {'sku': 'PROD-002', 'name': 'Widget B', 'price': 14.99},
        {'sku': 'PROD-001', 'name': 'Widget A', 'price': 9.99},  # Duplicate!
    ],
    'vendor_b': [
        {'sku': 'PROD-002', 'name': 'Widget B', 'price': 15.50},  # Different price!
        {'sku': 'PROD-003', 'name': 'Widget C', 'price': 7.99},
        {'sku': 'PROD-004', 'name': 'Widget D', 'price': 22.00},
    ],
    'vendor_c': [
        {'sku': 'prod-001', 'name': 'Widget A', 'price': 10.50},  # Lowercase SKU!
        {'sku': 'PROD-005', 'name': 'Widget E', 'price': 18.00},
    ]
}

# Get all unique SKUs (normalized to uppercase)
all_skus = {
    product['sku'].upper()
    for feed in vendor_feeds.values()
    for product in feed
}
print(f"Unique SKUs: {sorted(all_skus)}")
# ['PROD-001', 'PROD-002', 'PROD-003', 'PROD-004', 'PROD-005']

# Find SKUs available from multiple vendors (conflict detection)
sku_vendors = {}
for vendor, products in vendor_feeds.items():
    for product in products:
        sku = product['sku'].upper()
        sku_vendors.setdefault(sku, set()).add(vendor)

conflicting_skus = {sku for sku, vendors in sku_vendors.items() if len(vendors) > 1}
print(f"Conflicting SKUs (multiple vendors): {conflicting_skus}")
# {'PROD-001', 'PROD-002'}  ← Need price reconciliation!
```

### Example 3: Log Entry Deduplication

```python
# Deduplicate log events (remove repeated identical errors)

from datetime import datetime

log_entries = [
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:01:00', 'level': 'ERROR', 'message': 'DB connection timeout', 'service': 'api'},
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:01:05', 'level': 'ERROR', 'message': 'DB connection timeout', 'service': 'api'},
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:01:10', 'level': 'ERROR', 'message': 'DB connection timeout', 'service': 'api'},
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:02:00', 'level': 'WARNING', 'message': 'High memory usage', 'service': 'worker'},
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:03:00', 'level': 'ERROR', 'message': 'API rate limit exceeded', 'service': 'api'},
    {'timestamp': '2024-01-15 10:03:05', 'level': 'ERROR', 'message': 'API rate limit exceeded', 'service': 'api'},
]

# Unique error TYPES (deduplicate by message + service)
unique_error_signatures = {
    (entry['level'], entry['message'], entry['service'])
    for entry in log_entries
    if entry['level'] in ('ERROR', 'WARNING')
}

print("Unique error signatures:")
for sig in unique_error_signatures:
    print(f"  [{sig[0]}] {sig[2]}: {sig[1]}")

# Count: original vs unique
total_errors = sum(1 for e in log_entries if e['level'] == 'ERROR')
unique_errors = len({
    (e['message'], e['service'])
    for e in log_entries
    if e['level'] == 'ERROR'
})
print(f"\nTotal error occurrences: {total_errors}")
print(f"Unique error types: {unique_errors}")
print(f"Noise ratio: {total_errors - unique_errors} duplicates suppressed")
```

### Example 4: Data Pipeline Deduplication

```python
# Remove duplicate records before database insert

# Records from multiple batch imports (may overlap)
batch_1 = [
    {'id': 'R001', 'name': 'Alice', 'score': 85},
    {'id': 'R002', 'name': 'Bob',   'score': 72},
    {'id': 'R003', 'name': 'Carol', 'score': 91},
]
batch_2 = [
    {'id': 'R002', 'name': 'Bob',   'score': 72},  # Duplicate!
    {'id': 'R004', 'name': 'Dave',  'score': 65},
    {'id': 'R005', 'name': 'Eve',   'score': 88},
]
batch_3 = [
    {'id': 'R001', 'name': 'Alice', 'score': 85},  # Duplicate!
    {'id': 'R005', 'name': 'Eve',   'score': 88},  # Duplicate!
    {'id': 'R006', 'name': 'Frank', 'score': 77},
]

all_records = batch_1 + batch_2 + batch_3
print(f"Total records before dedup: {len(all_records)}")

# Get unique IDs using set comprehension
seen_ids = set()
unique_records = []
for record in all_records:
    if record['id'] not in seen_ids:
        seen_ids.add(record['id'])
        unique_records.append(record)

print(f"Unique records after dedup: {len(unique_records)}")

# OR: get just the set of unique IDs for EXISTS check before insert
unique_ids = {record['id'] for record in all_records}
print(f"Unique IDs: {sorted(unique_ids)}")
# ['R001', 'R002', 'R003', 'R004', 'R005', 'R006']

# Use in production: before inserting, check which IDs already exist
# existing_ids = {row['id'] for row in db.execute("SELECT id FROM records")}
# new_records = [r for r in batch if r['id'] not in existing_ids]
```

### Example 5: Tag and Category Deduplication

```python
# Content management: deduplicate tags across articles

articles = [
    {'title': 'Python Tips',       'tags': ['python', 'coding', 'tips', 'Python']},
    {'title': 'Data Science Intro','tags': ['data', 'Python', 'ML', 'data science']},
    {'title': 'Web Dev Guide',     'tags': ['html', 'css', 'javascript', 'coding']},
    {'title': 'AI Fundamentals',   'tags': ['AI', 'ML', 'Python', 'deep learning']},
]

# All unique normalized tags across all articles
all_tags = {
    tag.strip().lower().replace(' ', '-')
    for article in articles
    for tag in article['tags']
}
print(f"All unique tags ({len(all_tags)}):")
print(sorted(all_tags))
# ['ai', 'coding', 'css', 'data', 'data-science', 'deep-learning',
#  'html', 'javascript', 'ml', 'python', 'tips']

# Normalize tags in each article
normalized_articles = [
    {
        **article,
        'tags': sorted({tag.strip().lower() for tag in article['tags']})
    }
    for article in articles
]

for a in normalized_articles:
    print(f"  {a['title']}: {a['tags']}")

# Tags used by multiple articles (popular tags)
tag_article_count = {}
for article in articles:
    for tag in {t.lower() for t in article['tags']}:
        tag_article_count[tag] = tag_article_count.get(tag, 0) + 1

popular_tags = {tag for tag, count in tag_article_count.items() if count > 1}
print(f"Popular tags (2+ articles): {popular_tags}")
# {'python', 'coding', 'ml'}
```
